A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MMLoP. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, references, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original MMLoP classification, domain-generalization, ablation, and sensitivity results across multiple datasets.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports computational-efficiency measurements and comparisons with further low-rank methods.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the proposed low-rank prompts, shared up-projection, symmetric consistency loss, and uniform drift correction remain unchanged. The added parameter-sharing footnote and terminology revisions clarify the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 11 recognition datasets, four ImageNet distribution shifts, and three task settings. The new efficiency and low-rank comparisons use retained dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: Table A2 adds DIP, Block-LoRA, and Comp-LoRA to the base-to-novel comparisons, substantially strengthening comparison with directly relevant low-rank competitors. CLIP-LoRA and the earlier comparator sets are retained; Table 6 additionally compares resource costs against eight baselines.

E3.justification: The new efficiency evaluation introduces single-A6000 profiling across 11 datasets, measuring peak VRAM, total training time, per-image training and inference latency, FPS, and GFLOP. This substantially extends evaluation beyond accuracy and parameter counts. Existing MMLoP splits, shot counts, backbones, and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 adds a resource-efficiency analysis testing whether the small parameter budget translates into memory and runtime benefits. Existing component ablations, loss comparisons, hyperparameter analyses, and shared-up-projection visualization are retained; their relocation does not constitute new analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging over three seeds, including the sensitivity tables. Neither adds confidence intervals, significance tests, error bars, or a changed repeated-run protocol.

E6.justification: v2 adds efficiency measurements and per-dataset results for DIP, Block-LoRA, and Comp-LoRA, whose average HMs are 76.91%, 78.82%, and 78.77%. Reported MMA/CoPrompt parameter counts change from 675K/4.74M to 581K/3.82M. Some plotted few-shot results also change: the ViT-B/32 EuroSAT dip between two and four shots disappears from Fig. 5 to Fig. A3. Retained accuracy and ablation tables remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(9) retain the same mathematical formulation, with no added formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations. Renaming the symmetric-loss label and briefly explaining UDC's computational cost do not revise the mathematical framework.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the claim that low-rank factorization acts as an implicit regularizer with an emphasis on compact capacity and complementary regularization. The introduction quantifies the retained majority-outperformance claim as 16 of 19 methods. The central 11.5K-parameter contribution and 79.70% HM claim remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds Pareto-frontier positioning, an explanation of training-time differences through baseline epoch budgets, and interpretations of the low-rank comparisons. New appendix discussion also generalizes the existing ablations more strongly than their tables support: Appendix D.2 claims consistent shared-up-projection HM benefits, although Table A4 shows declines on several datasets.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability URL, identifies the single-GPU profiling hardware, reports resource measurements, and discusses baseline epoch budgets. A footnote clarifies the default shared-factor parameterization. The existing MMLoP implementation recipe remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The new low-rank related-work discussion distinguishes weight-space adaptation from prompt-space adaptation and explicitly positions MMLoP against DIP, Comp-LoRA, Block-LoRA, and existing CLIP-LoRA variants. This substantially expands discussion of the closest competing approaches beyond v1's general VLM and prompt-learning review.

P1.justification: Related Work moves from Appendix A to Section 2, while the learned-up-projection analysis moves into the appendix. The supplement is reorganized into Sections A–D with explanatory subsections. Additional edits refine the abstract, conclusion, method explanations, and terminology distinguishing low-rank prompting from backbone LoRA.

P2.justification: v2 adds efficiency Table 6 and comparison Table A2, relocates Fig. 3 as Fig. A1, and redraws the few-shot curves as Figs. A2–A3 with revised colors, grids, and axis formatting. Most existing table structures and the main method diagrams remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new resource measurements and directly relevant low-rank comparisons strengthen evidence for the paper's central efficiency argument, while clearer positioning and a code-availability statement improve documentation. However, new interpretations introduce overstatements: Section 5.5 calls MMLoP the lowest-parameter method despite CoOp's smaller count in Table 6, and Appendix D.2 claims consistent benefits contradicted by Table A4. The additions provide a useful but limited net quality gain.
